headline: Zscaler stock jumps 20% on report that CrowdStrike in talks to buy security vendor
author: Samantha Subin

paragraphs.text: Zscaler shares surged 20% in extended trading on Friday after Bloomberg reported that CrowdStrike is in talks to buy the cybersecurity vendor.
CrowdStrike shares fell 4% after the bell.
CrowdStrike declined to comment on the report. Zscaler didn't immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.
The talks between the two cyber vendors are ongoing, Bloomberg reported, citing sources familiar in the matter.

CrowdStrike has been one of the big cybersecurity winners in the AI boom, with its stock about doubling in value this year, lifting its market cap to $235 billion. Zscaler, meanwhile, is down 13% this year, pushing its market cap down to about $32 billion.
The potential deal would create one of the largest cybersecurity companies to date, behind cyber consolidator Palo Alto Networks, which closed Friday at a nearly $282 billion market cap.
Like its rival, CrowdStrike has made a slew of acquisitions in recent months to beef up security offerings in the AI era.
Most recently, CrowdStrike announced plans to acquire agentic observability platform Fiddler AI and AI trust platform Dreadnode.
